claims.text: FeCoNiCrMn high-entropy-alloy multilayers resist time-dependent plastic deformation.
Multiple interfaces hinder thermally activated dislocation climb in these multilayers.
Interfaces restrict continuous dislocation motion during creep.
Multiple interfaces interrupt dislocation pathways and suppress cross-interface dislocation climb.
Dislocations in multilayer architectures must traverse numerous interfaces.
The interfaces act as barriers that limit dislocation climb.
Limiting dislocation climb reduces the overall rate of plastic deformation.
Homogeneous FeCoNiCrMn films offer less resistance to dislocation climb than multilayer films.
Homogeneous films consequently accumulate more creep strain than multilayer films under similar conditions.
At approximately 400 degrees Celsius, multilayers will exhibit a significantly lower frequency of dislocation-climb events than homogeneous films.
Multilayers will exhibit lower dislocation mobility than homogeneous films.
Reduced climb activity and mobility will correlate with a lower creep-strain accumulation rate.
Interface-mediated climb suppression is expected to dominate when creep is controlled by dislocation climb, particularly near 400 degrees Celsius under constant-load conditions.
The influence of interface-mediated climb suppression may diminish outside the stated temperature and loading regime or when other deformation mechanisms dominate.
Interface quality and interfacial defect density may affect the proposed creep response.
Diffusional creep may operate concurrently with dislocation-climb-mediated creep.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies constant-stress creep, whereas the conditions specify constant mechanical load. Constant load and constant stress are not generally equivalent as specimen geometry changes during creep.
